chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, and Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, who said:
Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) said to me: 'The repeating is regarding the first two Rak'at, and the omission is (allowed) during the last two Rak'at.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on repeating prayer if an error occurs in the first versus the last two Rak'at?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) establishes a key jurisprudential distinction in Shia fiqh regarding the validity of prayer based on the timing of the error. It clarifies that mistakes in the first two Rak'at necessitate a full repetition (I'adha) due to the foundational nature of these units, whereas errors in the final two are treated as minor oversights (Sahw) that do not invalidate the prayer. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on precision in the initial stages of worship while maintaining ease in its conclusion.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahman Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, and Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa who said,
‘Abu Al-Hassan Al-Rezaasws said: ‘The repeating is regarding the first two Rak’at, and the omission is (allowed) during the last two Rak’at’ (i.e. no need to repeat).
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ and al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ who has said the following:
“Abu al-Hassan, al-Rida, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said to me, ‘In the first two Rak‘at it is performing again and confusion in the second two Rak‘at (has remedies).”’
